role.altitude: Her week is still the tray in the room, the ward or the car, the check in her hand, and the payment she takes. She stops re-adding a column when item, quantity, price and VAT code are already stored.
skills_to_grow: See that the tray matches the ticket before the total is shown
Leave a blank price or a blank VAT code off the draft and add that line herself
Take the payment in the room even when the total is already on the slip
Tell a missing item from a wrong price
role.ambitious_version: She still presents every check and still takes every payment. A delivery with a blank line is added by hand, and the draft total is never treated as the closed check.

tasks.short: Total the check, present it, and take payment.

steps.what: Match the tray in hand to the delivery ticket.
Total the stored lines into a draft check figure.
Check the draft names the items just handed over.
Present that check to the customer for these services.
Accept the payment customers offer for these services.
Write the accepted payment on the checks she closed.

tasks.design: The point-of-sale record in {OTHER} totals item, quantity, price and VAT code into a draft check only when those fields are already stored. She checks that the draft names what she handed over, then presents the check and takes the payment herself, and she writes the payment on the closed check. The total does not take the payment, and nothing sends a bill or an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The lines sat on a paper ticket, and the VAT rate was looked up item by item while she stood in the room.
tasks.enabler_now: A point-of-sale record can total stored lines from a VAT code already held on each item. That is configuration of the register, not a new way of taking the money.
tasks.still_hard: A patient, a resident or a passenger often does not pay on a screen. A blank price or a blank VAT code still has to be added by her, and she still has to see that the tray matches the ticket.
tasks.human_edge: She is the person who saw the tray leave her hands and who takes the cash, the card or the room charge in front of the customer.
tasks.altitude: She stops re-adding a complete bill. She still decides the tray matches the lines, still presents the check, and still takes the payment.

reach.task: Record the item and quantity that left the pass for this delivery.
reach.learn: Which of item, quantity, price and VAT code must be filled, or the draft total stays blank and she adds the check herself.

evidence.claim: Lightspeed Order Anywhere lets a guest scan a code, read item and allergen text, order and pay, and sends the order to the kitchen through the POS. That shows a register can hold the order and a total. This task does not remove presenting the check or taking payment, because the server still does both in a room, a ward or a car. The vendor's figure of about 8% more transactions, and the Fitzbillies 20% spend figure, are sales figures, not time on this task.

The drinks VAT page sets 21% on the alcoholic part and 9% on the rest only when those drinks are also sold unmixed and the prices add up. The draft total uses the VAT code stored on the item. It does not calculate that split itself.
The tax office wants a reliable register, preferably a certified checkout mark, and a seven-year retention. The closed check stays in that register. She does not keep a second archive.

A per-server sales log in the checkout can be a facility that monitors performance, so the works council must consent. Recording the payment on the check is the register. The design does not add a scoreboard of her sales.
The range is a scenario for room, ward and car service, not a published percentage. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Order-line fields are item name, quantity, unit price and VAT code. The producer is whoever took the order before this task, on the point-of-sale record or on a ticket that was keyed earlier. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
If item, quantity, price or VAT code is blank, the total step does not run and she adds the check by hand. A blank does not invent a price.
Matching the tray, presenting the check, accepting the payment and writing the closed check stay at full time. The only shortened step is adding the stored lines.
The draft total is not the closed check. She writes the payment only after the customer has paid. A later void is a new write, and the old acceptance does not cover it.
Nothing sends the bill to a finance system, and nothing raises an alert. There is no sheet to fill.

Upkeep is 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for a stored price or VAT code that she has to correct before she presents the check. Reading the draft for a wrong item is already in the check step and is not deducted again.
unknowns: What share of these deliveries already have item, quantity, price and VAT code stored before she arrives.
Whether a room or ward charge is written by her or by a cashier after she leaves.
research_questions: On a sample of room, ward and car deliveries, how often is the line complete before she totals it?
Do residents and patients pay at the bedside, or is the check a charge to the room or the ward?

already_counted.description: Read the draft for an item she did not hand over.

incremental.description: Correct a stored price or VAT code before she presents the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a delivery where item, quantity, price and VAT code are filled and the tray matches, she skips adding the column. On a blank line, a tray that does not match, or a bill she re-adds, the saving is near zero. Presenting the check, taking the payment and writing the closed check are not shortened. The figure is not a published sales lift.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
